clue.text: Up in the air as start of seminar's one-sided

definitions.note: the clue words describe being raised up, as if on stilts

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from seminar's

parts.note: something tilted leans one way, as a biased debate favours one side

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a seminar was one-sided from the outset and left matters unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' looks like 'undecided', but here it means raised on stilts; the more familiar sense of the answer is stiff or awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, the word describes something mounted on stilts and so raised high above the ground.

clue.text: Dusky seraglio maiden with skin blemish

indicators.note: a maiden is a first, as in a maiden voyage, so the opening letter of seraglio is taken

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned harem girl with a spot on her skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a harem woman, but it signals the first letter, as in maiden voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word means dark or swarthy, a synonym for dusky.

clue.text: I retain woeful sluggishness

indicators.note: woeful means poor or wretched, so the letters are in a bad state and rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: I keep a miserable lethargy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay inactive, a synonym for lethargy.

clue.text: Weed invading this catchment area

indicators.note: the answer invades the following words, lying hidden within them

explanation.surface: A weed spreading across a drainage basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tares are vetches, and in the Bible the word names a weed sown among wheat.

clue.text: Needs the nice man to be cast to support long time comic lead

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A casting call: the pleasant actor is needed to back up a long-serving comedy star.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis the Menace is the long-running mischievous boy on the front of the British comic The Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: This Beano character has led the British children's weekly since 1951, a comic hero of long standing.

clue.text: Feature of Mars clearly visible at end of robotic space relay

indicators.note: at the end of robotic means only its closing pair of letters is kept, the front dropped
relay is read as lay again, here laying the word space down backwards

explanation.surface: A rover's camera beams back a picture of the Martian poles, sent on through a robotic space relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relay' is a reversal signal here, turning SPACE into ECAPS; it is not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars has frozen polar caps of water and carbon dioxide, a well-known surface feature seen through telescopes.

clue.text: Tales about knight's folly? Die!

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all the letters of the word are used, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A curse on a knight's foolishness, read as stories of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's cycle of poems about King Arthur and his knights, so the surface is close to the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's work is a set of narrative poems, so it is a sequence of stories about the Round Table.

clue.text: Link established quite recently with a sort of kangaroo found down under

parts.note: the euro is another name for the wallaroo, a kind of kangaroo
a tunnel is something found deep beneath the ground

explanation.surface: A new connection is made with a kind of Australian marsupial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, where the euro lives, but here it describes the underground passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail connection beneath the Channel between Britain and France opened in 1994.

clue.text: Style displayed by a retired European senior army man

parts.note: rtd is the standard abbreviation for retired
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A retired European army officer shows off his fashion sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1920s and 1930s design movement is a recognised decorative mode, an example of an artistic style.

clue.text: South America beset by cutback in marriage

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the next piece goes around

parts.note: the clue word splits as a word meaning prune, lop, followed by back, so lop is written back to front
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: South America is besieged by spending cuts in its marriage of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like one place and 'cutback' like one word; both must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: Spousal as a noun, now chiefly plural, means nuptials or a wedding.

clue.text: Deviance by nearby car is the subject of worry

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake and tug it about, so these letters are worried into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver frets that a car parked nearby is behaving oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worry' means worrying at something as a dog does a bone, shaking it into a new shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a departure from what is normal or expected; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Reduced rate looks like 10 to be in proportion

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of rate is dropped

parts.note: the letters I and O printed together resemble the figure 10

explanation.surface: A cut rate is said to resemble the number ten, keeping things in proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is a visual trick: capital I beside capital O looks like the number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is one sense of proportion.

clue.text: Carry into temptation

indicators.note: the clue's into is split as in plus to, and in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to lead someone toward temptation, as in the Lord's Prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'into' as 'in to': 'in' is the signal, and the answer runs across 'to temptation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is to lug or haul it around, a synonym for carry.

clue.text: Mail takes meandering terrestrial river out

indicators.note: meandering means wandering this way and that, so the letters are rearranged
out says the river's letter is taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Post sent overland follows a winding river route.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an R (river) from TERRESTRIAL, as 'out' says, and rearrange what remains, as 'meandering' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Air letters were lightweight prepaid sheets folded into envelopes for cheap airmail, so they are a kind of post.

clue.text: Quiz overlord needs to be careful

parts.note: a master is a lord or ruler over others
to mind is to take care, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: A ruling power must stay cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running British TV quiz show with a famous black chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's well-known general-knowledge contest goes by this name, so it is an example of a quiz.

clue.text: Eastern European receives similar to 23 later on

definitions.note: the clue refers to the answer at 23 down, molten rock, after it has cooled

indicators.note: receives means the first word takes in the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a Balt is someone from the Baltic states
as means like or similar to

explanation.surface: A man from the east of Europe is given something comparable to the entry at 23.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is LAVA; when lava cools it hardens into this dark volcanic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: This volcanic rock forms when molten rock from an eruption cools and solidifies, so it is what that material becomes.

clue.text: Now redetermined to end self-inflicted harm

indicators.note: redetermined suggests settling again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a goal is an aim or end

explanation.surface: Someone resolves afresh to stop hurting themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, this football term means an action that backfires on whoever did it.

clue.text: A number of Italians accept a first round where there are lots of seats

definitions.text: where there are lots of seats

indicators.note: accept means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: tre is Italian for three, a number an Italian would use
a heat is a preliminary round of a race

explanation.surface: Some Italians agree to a first round in a crowded venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Italians' is not a crowd of them: it is a number in Italian, TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is an auditorium filled with rows of seating for an audience.

clue.text: Fearsome weapon's explosive includes dire cocktail

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, an explosive

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of dire are mixed

explanation.surface: A frightening weapon whose payload contains a deadly mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is a three-pronged spear and also the UK's nuclear missile system.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-pronged spear, and the British submarine nuclear missile, are both formidable arms.

clue.text: Leader changed purpose and direction of international agreement

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for purpose is swapped for another

parts.note: intent means purpose
E for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A leader alters aim and course regarding a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Attempt to get one's aim in

indicators.note: to get here means the first word acquires the second, holding it inside

parts.note: try means attempt
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An encouragement to try to get one's goal in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the final word 'in', meaning fashionable, which the surface hides as a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use, being in means being currently fashionable, a synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Not at all bright but a good looker possessing much attraction

indicators.note: possessing means the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person

indicators.note: much of a word is most of it, so its first letter goes

parts.note: pull means attraction or appeal

explanation.surface: Someone attractive but dim, holding plenty of allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much attraction' gives ULL, most of PULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat dull means dim or lacking brilliance, the opposite of bright.

clue.text: Arbitrates to get decent rise distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A mediator steps in to get a fair pay rise shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to step in on behalf of others, mediating between parties.

clue.text: Staff starting to come over in duffel coats

indicators.note: to come over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Office staff, beginning work, arrive dressed in duffel coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is the musical stave: its five lines begin with this symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation this symbol sits at the start of each stave, fixing the pitch of the lines.

clue.text: Stink thereof bubbles up after he leaves

indicators.note: bubbling stirs things about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves means the word he goes out of the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A bad smell rises from it once a man has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HE out of THEREOF ('he leaves') and rearrange TREOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetor is a strong foul smell, a synonym for stench.

clue.text: Termination of conflict with Russia a hot issue

indicators.note: termination means the closing part of the word, so its front is removed

parts.note: Balaclava was a Crimean War battle against Russia, site of the Charge of the Light Brigade

explanation.surface: Ending a war with Russia is a burning political question.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the end of BALACLAVA is used: drop BALAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock flowing from a volcano is, literally, a very hot substance issuing out.

clue.text: Boredom in the middle of Lent after dark in France is endless

indicators.note: the middle of a word is all but its outer letters, here from Lent
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: nuit is French for night, the dark

explanation.surface: Mid-Lent in France, after nightfall, the dullness seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go middle of LENT first, then NUI(T).
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names listless weariness, a synonym for tedium.

clue.text: Richard Adams, for instance, is beginning this after turning over leaf

indicators.note: after places is and the first of this behind the turned leaf
turning over means the word is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or the blade of a leaf

indicators.note: beginning means the opening letter of this is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about the author starting a fresh page.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Adams wrote Watership Down, a novel about rabbits; Chambers defines an animalist as a writer or painter of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An author whose subjects are animals, as in Watership Down, is one sense of this word.

clue.text: Play casually on the river Lune's banks

parts.note: the Tweed is a river on the border between England and Scotland

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so the outer letters of Lune are kept

explanation.surface: Someone strums idly by the banks of the Lune, a river in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweedle is to play an instrument idly or carelessly, a near synonym of noodle.

clue.text: Called back to get a seemingly feminist novel accompanying 4 down

definitions.note: the clue points to the dog that goes everywhere with the comic hero at 4 down

indicators.note: to get here means the first piece acquires the second inside it
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
She is H. Rider Haggard's novel, whose title sounds feminist

explanation.surface: Someone was rung to fetch a novel that appears feminist, to go with a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is Dennis the Menace, a long-running British comic character; his dog is named after its teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beano character Dennis is always accompanied by his toothy dog, which bears this name.
